title: Underlying coherent localization of a dg model enhancement
statement:
Use cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], coherent functors and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and derived chain enrichment and enriched localization of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. Work in fixed universes large enough for the categories below. Let $\mathcal M$ be a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups. Locally presentable means that for some infinite regular cardinal it is generated under the corresponding filtered colimits by a small family of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve those colimits. The enriched Hom complexes have unital associative chain-map compositions and the ordinary morphisms as their degree-zero cycles. Tensors and cotensors satisfy the natural complex adjunctions $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(K\otimes A,B)\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(K,\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,B))\cong\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,B^K)$. Suppose retract-closed classes $C,F,W$ satisfy two-out-of-three for $W$, and $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are functorial weak factorization systems generated by sets: every map factors into the two indicated classes, and those classes are exactly each other's diagonal-lifting classes. Assume that for $i:A\to B$ in $C$ and $p:X\to Y$ in $F$ the map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,X)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,X)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,Y)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,Y)$$
is degreewise surjective, and is a quasi-isomorphism if $i$ or $p$ lies in $W$. Let $\ell:\mathcal M\to\mathcal D$ be its enriched localization at $W$, and let $U\mathcal D$ have mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)}(\mathbf Z[0],\mathcal D(x,y))$.

The induced functor $q:N(\mathcal M)\to U\mathcal D$ is a universal homotopy coherent localization of the ordinary nerve at $W$. Precisely, for every infinity category $\mathcal E$, precomposition induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Fun}(U\mathcal D,\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{W}(N(\mathcal M),\mathcal E),$$
where the right side is the full subcategory of functors sending the arrows of $W$ to equivalences. This equivalence includes all coherent natural transformations and their higher homotopies.

The stated generalization is agent-formulated, not claimed verbatim from those propositions.
